title: The booking-confirmation decision is placed in rwb-decision while DP-04 and the registry story keep the evaluation in the owning service and state that rwb-decision never evaluates
source: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line (service rwb-decision, patterns DP04, secondary true); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04; RWB-E2-007 sections 4 and 12; Architecture v5 slide 27 through the P7 context pack
description: The Work Package fixes rwb-decision as the service of this slice and includes DP-04 with its C dependency on this service's own rule-package contract, so the slice evaluates package BOOKING_MATCH in rwb-decision. DP-04 and Arch v5 slide 27 keep governance central in rwb-decision and evaluation local in the one service that owns each model, and the P7 registry story RWB-P7-E2042-APP states in its section 19 that it never evaluates a package, so the sources do not settle whether rwb-decision evaluates this package or only holds its rows while another service evaluates it.
evidence: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line (service rwb-decision, patterns [DP01, DP03, DP04, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP19], legacy RWB-E2-007, secondary true); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-04 ('embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision'); RWB-E2-007 section 4 step 5 (RuleEvaluator.evaluate('BOOKING_MATCH', facts, D)) and section 12 (the evaluator is P3's published interface); P7 context pack slide 27 and 3 (approvals, rules and the log; 50 bank-wide rules apply at every step).
owner_role: Solution architect, with the decision service owner
proposed: Keep the Work Package placement: this slice evaluates BOOKING_MATCH on the version it holds, through the embedded kit, and publishes the outcome; the treatment state, the task, the route move and the posting stay with their owners. Record the placement in the Change Register so the registry story's boundary is restated once.

title: The operation set, paths and payloads of the batch, account, treatment, task, parameter and list contracts, the decision code, the record's snapshot and actions shape and several read and message details are in no source
source: RWB-E2-007 sections 11, 12 and 14; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2 and A2.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-06, DP-07 and DP-11
description: The legacy story gives six Java interfaces and two endpoints, not REST contracts, and no source enumerates the target operations, their payloads or their field names for the batch read, the account snapshot, the approved-not-booked read, the booking and difference write, the task request, the parameters and the lists. No source states which LOV-DECISION code a booking decision carries, the physical shape of inputs_ref and of the actions payload, the filters of the decisions read beyond the four named, the page size and ordering, or the text of MSG-GEN-006, so those values stand as the placeholder and the shapes are carried as the legacy interfaces restated.
evidence: RWB-E2-007 section 12 (TreatmentQuery.approvedNotBooked, TreatmentCommands.markBooked and recordBookingDifference, RuleEvaluator.evaluate, AccountQuery.forCase, BatchStatusQuery.forSource, TaskApi.raiseTask; POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun; GET /api/recovery/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}); section 11 (the field IDs of treatment, v_ace_account, v_ace_batch_status, task and reconciliation_result); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry columns) and T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT only); FSD P7 v3 A2.3 (the seven field groups of an entry).
owner_role: Solution architect, with the owners of rwb-integration, rwb-treatment and rwb-case
proposed: Take the operation set from the six legacy interfaces, publish each on the per-service base of DP-13 with one hop and a 2 s timeout, take the decision code and the outcome values from LOV-DECISION and the reference lists in force, put the account facts of the business date in inputs_ref and the difference terms and unbooked accounts in actions, and fix the read filters, the page size, the ordering and the MSG-GEN-006 text with their owners before SIT.

title: No source names the event that carries a booking decision out of rwb-decision, because the legacy TreatmentBooked is rwb-payment's and is raised after the treatment is booked
source: RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 12 and 17; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14; P7 context pack ownership rows (EV-08, EV-09, EV-30)
description: The legacy story consumes TreatmentApproved (EV-10) and relies on rwb-payment to publish TreatmentBooked (EV-11) and on rwb-case to publish CaseStateChanged (EV-05) once the treatment is booked. In the target the decision leaves rwb-decision before any of those happen, and no source names the rwb-decision event, its payload or its key, while the P7 ownership rows name only EV-08, EV-09 and EV-30 for this service.
evidence: RWB-E2-007 section 4 steps 6 to 8 and section 12 ('Events published: TreatmentBooked (EV-11) by P8 ... CaseStateChanged (EV-05) by P3'); section 17 (no personal data in events); Template and Rules v1 R4 (event name rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1) and R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14; P7 context pack ownership rows Events (EV-08, EV-09, EV-30).
owner_role: Solution architect, with the event platform owner
proposed: Publish one rwb.decision.BookingDecisionMade.v1 per treatment and business date on rwb.decision.events.v1, keyed by treatmentId, carrying the outcome, the row, the package code and version, the business date and the difference terms, and leave TreatmentBooked, CaseStateChanged and the posting with their owners.

title: The eleven patterns add seven platform build dependencies and four consumed contracts that the metadata rows of a secondary slice do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-03, DP-04, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-19) and R5.4; P7 context pack ownership rows; Work Package B2-P7-021 story line (H [], C [RWB-P2-E2007-CON], I [], X [])
description: The patterns the Work Package fixes add H rows RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the C rows RWB-P7-E1073-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON plus the treatment and task contracts, while the story line fixes Depends on (build) empty and RWB-P2-E2007-CON as the only contract dependency. The metadata rows are written exactly as the Work Package fixes them and the added rows are carried in sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and 13.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), DP-04 (H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON), DP-06 (H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON), DP-07 (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON), DP-09 (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), DP-10 (H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) and DP-19 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the Work Package fixes H [], C [RWB-P2-E2007-CON], I [], X [] and marks the slice secondary.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the delivery lead
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the Work Package fixes them, name every added row in the pattern table and the fakes of 12.8, build against the published contracts and fakes from Day 1, and let step D1 decide whether the seven H rows and the four consumed contracts enter the dependency map.

title: The name of the rwb-decision database login is in no source
source: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; P7 context pack naming rules
description: Template and Rules R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service and no document states the login name, its role name or its credential scope, so the story uses the phrase 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' and registers the value as missing.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R4 (one login per service) and R5.5 DP-02 (recovery_svc login becomes one login per service); P7 context pack 'Naming and shared platform rules' names the schema, the base, the topic, the queue and the Java package, and no login.
proposed: Let the ACE team allocate the login with the schema rwb_decision and record it in the platform secret store; the story keeps the phrase until it is allocated.

title: A secondary slice with an empty acceptance-criteria list owns no legacy criterion while its eleven legacy test cases are kept, and the legacy levels have no counterpart in the template
source: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line (secondary true, acs []); Template and Rules v1 R5.7, R7.2 s7 and s16; RWB-E2-007 sections 7 and 16
description: The story line fixes acs empty, so the nine legacy criteria of RWB-E2-007 belong to the slices that own the treatment, the case, the payment and the screens, while the eleven legacy test case IDs are carried in tcs_legacy and kept. The Covers column therefore names this slice's new criteria and the rules they prove, and the mapping from the legacy System, Access and Resilience levels to the levels of R7.2 is a ruling of this story.
evidence: Work Package B2-P7-021 story line (acs [], tcs_legacy TC-E2-007-10 then TC-E2-007-01 to TC-E2-007-09 and TC-E2-007-11); RWB-E2-007 section 7 (AC1 to AC9) and section 16 (eleven test cases, Level System, Access and Resilience); Template and Rules v1 R5.7 rule 2 and R7.2 s16.
proposed: Keep the eleven legacy test case IDs in the order the Work Package fixes with the Covers column naming this slice's criteria, map System to Component, Access to Contract and Resilience to NFR, and leave the legacy criteria with the slices that own them and with RWB-ITG-E2007-ITG.

title: The timezone, overlap, retry and fallback of the JOB-08 run and the behaviour of the legacy feature flag when off are in no source
source: RWB-E2-007 sections 3, 4, 5 and 13; Architecture v5 slides 44 and 28 through the P7 context pack; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10
description: The legacy story starts JOB-08 on AceDataReady for ALS and allows a rerun, and no source states the timezone of the run, the overlap and catch-up policy, the retry and backoff of a failed gate, whether a fallback sweep Schedule exists, the names of the properties that carry them, or what a caller sees when the legacy flag rwb.integration.booking-confirmation is off.
evidence: RWB-E2-007 section 4 step 1 (JOB-08 starts when AceDataReady (EV-26) arrives for ALS with business date D), section 5 X4 and X5 (a batch that is not COMPLETE; a rerun for the same date), section 12 (restart through POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun) and section 13 (feature flag rwb.integration.booking-confirmation); Architecture v5 slide 44 (schedules) through the context pack; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the workflow platform owner
proposed: Run the event-started BookingConfirmationWorkflow on queue rwb-decision at Asia/Bangkok, one run per business date with a second start refused with MSG-P2-006 and a failed gate retried on the next AceDataReady for the date, create no fallback Schedule, and let the flag off stop the start while the records already written stay readable.

title: The legacy run writes the REC-03 result to reconciliation_result, and no table or owner of that name exists in the target and no source assigns the break list
source: RWB-E2-007 sections 4, 5, 11 and 14; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17
description: The legacy story ends each run by writing the counts of treatments read, booked, missing and differing to reconciliation_result (DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129) for the REC-03 break list and the data steward. TSD P7 v2 declares no such table, no ownership row names it, and DP-17 removes the data lake and moves reporting to rwb-reporting read models built from events, so neither the table, its fields nor the report owner is settled for the target.
evidence: RWB-E2-007 section 4 step 9 (the run summary and the REC-03 result to reconciliation_result), section 5 (the REC-03 break list), section 11 (DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129, reconciliation_result) and section 14; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (decision_log_entry and the registry tables only); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17 and DP-09.
owner_role: Solution architect, with the reporting owner
proposed: Create no reconciliation_result table in rwb_decision: publish each decision and its outcome, serve the counts from decision_log_entry on the read of 12.1, and let rwb-reporting build the REC-03 break list from the events, with the field IDs carried as values until that owner names its read model.
